examples.en: The size doesn't fit, so I'm exchanging the clothes.

examples.ko: 어제 산 신발을 다른 색으로 교환했어요.
examples.en: I exchanged the shoes I bought yesterday for another color.

examples.ko: 이 상품은 일주일 안에 교환하실 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can exchange this item within a week.
I swapped phone numbers with my friend and said goodbye.
If you have the receipt, we'll exchange it right away.
Which counter do I go to for an exchange?

explain: 교환은 다른 물건으로 바꾸는 것이고 '환불'은 돈을 돌려받는 것이라서, 가게에서는 둘을 꼭 구분해서 말해요. 일상에서는 '바꾸다'도 같이 쓰지만 가게 규정에는 '교환'이 나와요. 전화번호나 선물처럼 서로 주고받을 때도 '교환하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 교환 means swapping for another item, while '환불' (refund) means getting money back, so shops keep the two clearly apart. Casual speech also uses '바꾸다', but store rules say 교환. It also works when two people give each other things, such as phone numbers or gifts.

examples.en: Our school goes on vacation next week.
Our school started vacation at the end of July.
When school breaks for vacation, I'll go to my hometown.
The kids are very excited because vacation starts tomorrow.
I took photos with my friends before vacation started.
It has been a week since vacation started.

explain: 주어는 학교나 학생이고, 직장인이 쉬는 건 '방학'이 아니라 '휴가'예요. 방학이 끝나고 학교가 다시 시작하는 건 '개학하다'라서 둘이 짝이에요. '방학 동안'처럼 명사 '방학'을 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: The subject is a school or students; office workers take '휴가' (leave), not 방학. When vacation ends and school starts again, you say '개학하다', so the two are a pair. The noun appears more often, as in '방학 동안' (during the break).

examples.en: I usually go out early in the morning.
It's raining, so I don't want to go out.
My mother has gone out for a moment.
Be sure to take an umbrella when you go out.
On weekends I rest at home and don't go out.
I went out and suddenly got caught in the rain.

explain: '나가다'가 가장 일상적이고, '외출하다'는 볼일이나 놀러 집 밖으로 나가는 일에 써요. 집에 없다는 말은 '외출 중이에요'라고 해요. 윗사람이 나갔을 때는 '외출하셨어요', 돌아오는 건 '돌아오다'나 '귀가하다'예요.
explain_en: '나가다' is the plainest word, and 외출하다 is for heading out of the house to run errands or have fun. 'I'm not home right now' is '외출 중이에요'. For someone senior you say '외출하셨어요', and coming back is '돌아오다' or the more formal '귀가하다'.

examples.en: I always read before I go to bed.
I read at a quiet cafe on the weekend.

examples.ko: 독서하는 시간이 하루 중에 제일 행복해요.
examples.en: Reading time is the happiest part of my day.
During vacation I want to spend the whole day reading.

examples.ko: 동생은 매일 한 시간씩 독서하기로 했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling decided to read for an hour every day.

examples.ko: 올해 독서한 책 중에 이 책이 제일 좋았어요.
examples.en: Of the books I read this year, this one was the best.

explain: 대화에서는 '책을 읽어요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '독서'는 '취미가 독서예요'처럼 명사로 쓰거나 '독서를 하다'로 많이 말해요. 신문이나 메시지처럼 책이 아닌 것에는 '독서'를 안 쓰고 '읽다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 동생이 독서삼매경에 빠져서 제가 불러도 몰라요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책에 푹 빠져서 다른 소리가 안 들릴 정도일 때 써요. 보통 '빠지다'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is so lost in a book that they don't hear anything else. It usually goes with the verb '빠지다' (to fall into).

explain_en: In conversation, '책을 읽어요' sounds much more natural. 독서 is mostly used as a noun, as in '취미가 독서예요' (my hobby is reading), or as '독서를 하다'. For things that aren't books, such as newspapers or messages, use '읽다', not 독서.

examples.en: Our club is recruiting new members.
The company recruited new employees.
I saw a notice recruiting volunteers.
Until when do you plan to recruit participants?
I'll let you know as soon as we recruit students.
I was surprised that more people signed up than expected.

explain: 사람을 구하는 쪽이 '모집하다'를 쓰고, 들어가려는 쪽은 '지원하다'를 써요. 회사가 최종으로 뽑아서 일을 시키는 건 '채용하다'예요. 광고에는 '신입 사원 모집'처럼 '하다' 없이 붙여 써요.
explain_en: The side looking for people uses 모집하다, and the side wanting to join uses '지원하다' (apply). When a company finally selects someone and hires them, that is '채용하다'. Ads drop 하다 and just say '신입 사원 모집'.

examples.en: I delete photos I don't need every day.
I deleted an important email by mistake.
You must not delete this file.
I deleted the app and installed it again.
To delete a message, press and hold it.

examples.ko: 삭제한 사진은 휴지통에서 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can find deleted photos in the trash.

explain: 손으로 쓴 글씨나 연필 자국은 '지우다'이고, 컴퓨터·휴대폰의 파일·사진·메시지는 '삭제하다'를 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '사진 지웠어요'도 자주 해요. 삭제한 걸 되살리는 건 '복구하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Handwriting and pencil marks are '지우다' (erase), while files, photos and messages on a computer or phone are usually 삭제하다. In speech people also say '사진 지웠어요'. Bringing back something you deleted is '복구하다'.

examples.en: I record the lesson every time.
I recorded it after getting the teacher's permission.
I'm going to a studio to record a song.
I recorded my voice and listened to it.
If you record the meeting, it's convenient later.

examples.ko: 지금 녹음하는 중이니까 조용히 해 주세요.
examples.en: We're recording right now, so please be quiet.

explain: '녹음하다'는 소리만 담는 일이고, 화면까지 담으면 '녹화하다'예요. 두 단어가 비슷해서 자주 헷갈려요. 녹음한 걸 '듣다', 녹화한 걸 '보다'라고 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: 녹음하다 captures sound only; if the picture is included it is '녹화하다'. The two are easy to mix up. A simple trick is that you '듣다' (listen to) a 녹음 and '보다' (watch) a 녹화.

examples.en: Please sign down here.
I signed the contract for my new place yesterday.
I pay by card and sign the receipt.
Please tell me where to sign.
Write your name and sign below.
You need an ID to sign.

explain: 일상에서는 '사인하다'도 많이 써요. 가수나 배우가 팬에게 해 주는 건 '서명'보다 '사인'이라고 해요. 도장을 찍는 건 '도장을 찍다'라고 따로 말해요.
explain_en: In daily life people also say '사인하다'. A singer or actor signing for a fan is usually '사인', not 서명. Stamping with a seal is a separate phrase, '도장을 찍다'.

examples.en: My parents allowed me to take the trip alone.

examples.ko: 선생님이 수업 중에 사진 찍는 것을 허락해요.
examples.en: The teacher allows taking photos during class.
Nobody has allowed it yet.

examples.ko: 사장님이 허락하면 내일 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the boss allows it, I can take tomorrow off.

examples.ko: 관리실에서 여기에 짐을 두는 것을 허락해 줬어요.
examples.en: The management office allowed us to leave our things here.
I'll wait until Dad gives permission.

explain: '허락'은 부모님·선생님 같은 사람이 해 주는 것이고, 관청이 내주는 건 '허가'예요. 해 주는 쪽은 '허락하다', 받는 쪽은 '허락을 받다'라고 해요. 친구 사이에서는 '허락' 대신 '해도 돼요?'라고 물어요.
explain_en: 허락 comes from a person such as a parent or teacher, while permission issued by an authority is '허가'. The giver says '허락하다' and the receiver says '허락을 받다'. Between friends people usually just ask '해도 돼요?' (may I?).

examples.en: I collect stamps as a hobby.
My younger sibling collected toys as a child.
I'm in the middle of collecting data for my paper.
I want to collect postcards while traveling.
We collected opinions with a survey and presented them.
I arranged the stamps I collected in an album.

explain: '모으다'가 일상 말이라서 돈·친구·사람은 '모으다'를 쓰고, '수집하다'는 취미나 자료·정보를 체계적으로 모을 때 써요. '돈을 모으다'는 되지만 '돈을 수집하다'는 어색해요. 물건을 수집하는 사람은 '수집가'라고 해요.
explain_en: '모으다' is the everyday word, so money or friends take 모으다, while 수집하다 is for collecting hobby items, materials or information in an organized way. '돈을 모으다' works, but '돈을 수집하다' sounds odd. A person who collects things is a '수집가'.

examples.ko: 보내기 전에 한 번 더 검토해요.
examples.en: I review it once more before sending.
I reviewed the plan carefully.
The team leader is reviewing the documents.
I'll look into whether there's a good way.
I'll contact you right after I've reviewed the contents.
There are so many documents to review that it's tiring.

explain: '확인하다'는 맞는지 보는 것이고, '검토하다'는 좋은지 나쁜지 따져 보고 결정하려고 살피는 거예요. 직장에서 '검토해 볼게요'는 바로 정하지 않겠다는 뜻일 때가 많아요. '검토 중이에요'처럼 '중'을 붙여 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '확인하다' is checking whether something is right, while 검토하다 is weighing the pros and cons in order to decide. At work, '검토해 볼게요' often means 'I won't decide right now'. People often add 중 and say '검토 중이에요' (it's under review).

examples.en: I make two copies of each contract.
I made a copy of my passport to give to the company.
You must not copy this book.
How much per page does it cost to make a copy?
I copied the file and put it on a USB drive.
I pasted the copied text into the email.

explain: 복사기로 종이를 복사하는 것도, 컴퓨터에서 복사해서 붙이는 것도 '복사하다'예요. 컴퓨터에서는 '복사하다'와 '붙여넣다'를 짝으로 써요. 남의 숙제를 그대로 따라 쓰는 건 '복사'가 아니라 '베끼다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Photocopying paper and copy-pasting on a computer are both 복사하다. On a computer it pairs with '붙여넣다' (paste). Copying someone else's homework word for word is '베끼다', not 복사.

examples.en: I attend class every day.
I was sick yesterday, so I couldn't attend.
Be sure to attend on the day of the exam.
We give a small gift to students who attend.
All the students are present today.
If you come every day, they give you a stamp.

explain: 학교·학원 수업에 나오는 건 '출석하다'이고, 회의나 결혼식 같은 행사에 가는 건 '참석하다'를 많이 써요. 반대말은 '결석하다'이고, 늦게 오면 '지각하다'예요. 선생님이 이름을 불러 확인하는 건 '출석을 부르다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Showing up for school or academy classes is 출석하다, while going to events such as meetings or weddings is usually '참석하다'. The opposite is '결석하다' (be absent), and arriving late is '지각하다'. A teacher calling names to check is '출석을 부르다'.

examples.en: This shop discounts clothes every weekend.
They discounted these clothes by 30 percent last week.
They give students a 10 percent discount.
If you discount the price, customers increase.
Do you give a discount if I pay by card?
I bought it at the discounted price, so I feel good.

explain: 가게가 정가를 내리는 건 '할인하다'이고, 손님이 값을 깎아 달라고 할 때는 '깎아 주세요'라고 해요. 시장에서는 '좀 깎아 주세요'가 흔한 말이에요. 내린 가격은 '할인가'라고 불러요.
explain_en: When a shop lowers the list price, that is 할인하다. When a customer asks for a lower price, they say '깎아 주세요' (please knock it down), which is common at markets. The reduced price is called '할인가'.

examples.ko: 고장 난 물건은 가게에서 환불해 줘요.
examples.en: The shop gives refunds for broken items.
I returned the bag I bought yesterday for a refund.
It's hard to get a refund without a receipt.
Where do I go to get a refund?
The shop refunded my money.
The refund period is one week.

explain: '환불'은 돈을 돌려받는 것이고 '교환'은 다른 물건으로 바꾸는 것이에요. 물건을 돌려보내는 건 '반품하다'라서 보통 '반품하고 환불받다' 순서로 말해요. 손님은 '환불받다', 가게는 '환불해 주다'라고 말하는 게 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 환불 means getting money back, while '교환' means swapping for another item. Sending the goods back is '반품하다', so people often say '반품하고 환불받다' in that order. It sounds natural for the customer to say '환불받다' and for the shop to say '환불해 주다'.

examples.en: I major in business at university.
My older sister majored in music at university.
What do you want to major in at university?
Many students major in Korean.
What work can you do if you major in art?
I want to work in the field I majored in.

explain: '공부하다'는 무엇이든 배울 때 쓰지만 '전공하다'는 대학에서 중심으로 배우는 한 분야에만 써요. 사람을 만나면 '전공이 뭐예요?'라고 자주 물어요. 전공을 두 개 하면 '복수 전공'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '공부하다' works for studying anything, but 전공하다 is only for the one main field you study at university. When meeting people, Koreans often ask '전공이 뭐예요?' (what's your major?). Having two majors is '복수 전공'.

examples.en: I study Korean a little every day.
Yesterday I studied new words with an app.
Studying alone can be boring at times.

examples.ko: 제가 학습하는 방법을 조금 바꿔 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried changing the way I study a little.
I'm studying grammar with this book.
I review what I studied every day.

explain: 말할 때는 '공부해요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '학습'은 교재·교육 자료·인공지능 설명 같은 글에서 자주 보여요. '학습 자료', '학습 계획'처럼 명사로 붙여 쓰는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: In speech '공부해요' sounds far more natural. 학습 shows up in textbooks, teaching materials and explanations of AI. It is often attached as a noun, as in '학습 자료' (study material) and '학습 계획' (study plan).

examples.en: I'm going to study in Korea next year.
My older sister studied in the United States when she was in college.
I want to study abroad, so I'm learning Korean.
I made many friends while studying abroad.
Which country would be good to study in?

examples.ko: 유학한 친구에게 그 나라 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard about that country from a friend who studied there.

explain: '한국에 유학하다'보다 '한국으로 유학을 오다', '미국에 유학을 가다'처럼 '가다/오다'와 같이 말하는 일이 더 많아요. 외국에서 공부하는 학생은 '유학생'이에요. 대학에서 한두 학기만 다녀오는 건 '교환 학생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: People more often say '한국으로 유학을 오다' or '미국에 유학을 가다' (with 가다/오다) than 유학하다 alone. A student studying abroad is a '유학생'. Going to a university abroad for just a semester or two is '교환 학생' (exchange student).

examples.en: I graduate this year and get a job right away.
My older brother got a job at a bank last year.
I want to get a job soon.
Getting a job isn't easy these days.

examples.ko: 한국 회사에 취직하면 비자를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you get a job at a Korean company, you can get a visa.
After I got a job, I gave my parents a gift.

explain: '취직하다'는 직장을 얻는 순간을 말하고, 이미 일하는 상태는 '일하다'나 '다니다'로 말해요. '회사에 다녀요'가 '회사에 취직해요'보다 지금 상태에 맞아요. '취업하다'도 비슷한데, 일자리를 얻는 일 전체에 더 넓게 써요.
explain_en: 취직하다 is the moment you land a job, while the ongoing state is '일하다' or '다니다' ('회사에 다녀요' fits better than '회사에 취직해요' for now). '취업하다' is close but covers getting work more broadly.

examples.en: I preview the new words before class.

examples.ko: 어제 저녁에 내일 배울 내용을 예습했어요.
examples.en: Yesterday evening I previewed what we'll learn tomorrow.
If you preview, class is easier.
I've developed a habit of previewing every day.

examples.ko: 수업 전에는 예습하고 수업 후에는 복습해요.
examples.en: I preview before class and review after class.
I had no time to prepare, so I just went.

explain: 수업 전에 미리 보는 건 '예습', 수업 후에 다시 보는 건 '복습'이라서 보통 '예습, 복습' 순서로 붙여 말해요. 숙제를 하는 건 예습도 복습도 아니고 '숙제하다'라고 해요. 학교보다 훨씬 앞선 내용을 미리 배우는 건 '선행 학습'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: Looking things over before class is '예습' and going over them again afterwards is '복습', and the two are usually said together in that order, '예습, 복습'. Doing homework is neither; it is '숙제하다'. Learning material far ahead of what school teaches is called '선행 학습' (advance learning).

examples.en: I'm talking on the phone with my friend at the office now.
I talked with my mother on the phone for an hour yesterday.
I'd like to talk on the phone for a moment; is now okay?
I'm on a call right now, so I'll phone you later.
I'm too busy today, so it's hard to talk on the phone.

examples.ko: 회의 때문에 오래 통화할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't talk on the phone for long because of the meeting.

explain: '전화하다'는 전화를 거는 행동이고, '통화하다'는 연결돼서 서로 말하는 데 초점이 있어요. 그래서 '통화 중이에요', '통화가 안 돼요'처럼 연결 상태를 말할 때도 많이 써요. 보통 '친구와 통화하다'처럼 '와/과'랑 같이 써요.
explain_en: '전화하다' is the act of making a call, while '통화하다' focuses on being connected and actually talking. That is why you also hear '통화 중이에요' (the line is busy) and '통화가 안 돼요' (I can't get through). It usually goes with '와/과', as in '친구와 통화하다'.

examples.ko: 반 친구들이 모두 새 친구를 환영해요.
examples.en: All the classmates welcome the new friend.
We warmly welcomed the new employee.
We held a party to welcome the guests.
I want to welcome the newly arrived student.
Fans gathered at the airport to welcome the singer.
Thank you so much for welcoming me like this.

explain: 손님이나 새로 온 사람을 맞이할 때 써요. 행사나 가게에서는 '환영합니다'라고 인사하지만, 일상에서는 '어서 오세요'가 더 흔해요. 의견이나 계획에도 쓰는데 '그 계획을 환영해요'는 뉴스나 회의처럼 딱딱한 말투예요.
explain_en: Use it when you greet guests or newcomers. Events and shops say '환영합니다', but in daily life '어서 오세요' is more common. It also works for plans or opinions, but '그 계획을 환영해요' sounds stiff, like news or a meeting.

examples.en: I buy books online.
I bought a new computer last week.
To buy a ticket, please line up over there.
Where did you buy that bag?

examples.ko: 이 제품은 매장에서만 구입할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy this product only in stores.
The clothes I bought were small, so I went to exchange them.

explain: '사다'와 뜻이 같지만 더 격식 있는 말이라 안내문, 쇼핑몰, 뉴스에서 자주 보여요. 친구와 말할 때는 '샀어요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 짝말은 파는 쪽의 '판매하다'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '사다' but sounds more formal, so you see it in notices, online shops and the news. With friends, '샀어요' is much more natural. Its counterpart on the seller's side is '판매하다'.

examples.en: I was really moved after watching the movie.

examples.ko: 친구가 쓴 편지를 읽고 감동한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I was once touched after reading a letter my friend wrote.
I was moved by the song and cried.
I'm easily moved even by small kindnesses.

examples.ko: 그 이야기를 읽으면 누구나 감동할 거예요.
examples.en: Anyone who reads that story will be moved.

examples.ko: 이런 선물에도 감동하지 않는 사람이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there anyone who isn't touched by a gift like this?

explain: 사람이 주어이면 '감동하다'나 '감동받다'를 쓰고, 영화나 이야기가 주어이면 '감동적이다'를 써요. '영화가 감동적이에요', '저는 감동했어요'처럼 짝을 맞춰 보세요. '감동을 받았어요'도 아주 자주 말해요.
explain_en: When a person is the subject, use '감동하다' or '감동받다'; when a movie or story is the subject, use '감동적이다'. Compare '영화가 감동적이에요' and '저는 감동했어요'. '감동을 받았어요' is also very common.

examples.en: I go sightseeing in Seoul with a friend on the weekend.
I went sightseeing on Jeju Island with my family.
There are many people sightseeing around here.
I want to go sightseeing around the city for a day.
You need a map to go sightseeing on foot.

examples.ko: 관광하러 온 외국인이 사진을 찍고 있어요.
examples.en: A foreigner who came sightseeing is taking photos.

explain: '관광하다'는 앞에 장소가 와서 '서울을 관광하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '구경하다'나 '여행하다'를 더 많이 말해요. 같은 한자어로 '관광지', '관광객', '관광버스'가 있어요.
explain_en: '관광하다' takes a place before it, as in '서울을 관광하다'. In everyday talk people say '구경하다' or '여행하다' more often. The same root gives '관광지' (tourist spot), '관광객' (tourist) and '관광버스' (tour bus).

examples.en: Please don't misunderstand what I said.
My friend completely misunderstood me.
People often misunderstand this word.
I'll explain in detail so there's no misunderstanding.
I'm sorry I misheard and misunderstood.
If you misunderstood my text message, I'm sorry.

explain: 사람의 마음이나 말을 잘못 받아들였을 때 써요. 명사 '오해'로 '오해를 풀다', '오해를 사다'처럼 쓰는 일도 많아요. '오해하지 마세요'는 아주 자주 쓰는 표현이라 통째로 외워 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: Use it when you take someone's feelings or words the wrong way. The noun '오해' is also common in '오해를 풀다' (clear up a misunderstanding) and '오해를 사다' (be misunderstood). '오해하지 마세요' is a very common expression, so it is worth memorizing as a whole.

examples.en: We decorate a tree together at Christmas.

examples.ko: 생일 파티를 위해 방을 꽃으로 장식했어요.
examples.en: I decorated the room with flowers for the birthday party.
A cake looks prettier if you decorate it with fruit.
I want to decorate the wall with pictures.

examples.ko: 집을 장식하는 데 시간이 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Decorating the house took a long time.
It's the day the students decorated the classroom.

explain: '장식하다'는 '꾸미다'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있고, 물건이나 공간에 주로 써요. 사람의 얼굴이나 옷차림에는 '꾸미다'를 써요. 방을 꾸밀 때는 '방을 꾸미다'도 아주 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '장식하다' is close to '꾸미다' but more formal and mostly used for objects and spaces. For a person's face or outfit, use '꾸미다'. For a room, '방을 꾸미다' is just as natural.

examples.ko: 요즘 학생들 사이에서 이 노래가 유행해요.
examples.en: This song is popular among students these days.
This style was really in fashion last year.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 지금 많이 유행하고 있어요.
examples.en: This outfit is very much in fashion now.
I tried a food that's trendy these days.

examples.ko: 이 춤은 곧 유행할 것 같아요.
examples.en: This dance looks like it will become popular soon.
The flu is going around, so please wear a mask.

explain: 노래, 옷, 음식뿐 아니라 독감처럼 퍼지는 병에도 '유행하다'를 써요. 하지만 가수나 배우 같은 사람에게는 쓰지 않고 '인기가 많다'라고 해요. '유행을 타다'처럼 명사 '유행'으로도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 이 모자는 유행을 타서 내년에는 못 쓸 것 같아요.
phrases.en: to be subject to trends; to go in and out of fashion
phrases.nuance_ko: 한때 인기가 있다가 시간이 지나면 사라지는 물건이나 스타일에 써요. 오래 입을 수 있는 옷은 '유행을 안 타요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things or styles that are popular for a while and then fade. Clothes that last are described as '유행을 안 타요'.
phrases.en_equiv: go in and out of fashion

explain_en: '유행하다' is used for songs, clothes and food, and also for spreading illnesses like the flu. It is not used for people such as singers or actors; for them say '인기가 많다'. The noun '유행' also appears in '유행을 타다'.

examples.en: I enjoy a film at home on the weekend.
I took my time looking at paintings at the art museum.
Listening to music is my hobby.
Please enjoy it quietly for the sake of others.
We talked after watching the performance.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 창밖 풍경을 감상하면서 커피를 마셨어요.
examples.en: On a rainy day I drank coffee while taking in the view out the window.

explain: 영화, 음악, 그림, 공연처럼 즐기면서 보고 듣는 대상에 써요. 일상적인 것에는 그냥 '보다', '듣다'를 써요. 취미를 말할 때 '영화 감상', '음악 감상'이라고 짧게 말하는 것도 아주 흔해요.
explain_en: Use it for things you watch or listen to for enjoyment: films, music, paintings, performances. For everyday seeing and hearing, just use '보다' and '듣다'. When talking about hobbies, short answers like '영화 감상' and '음악 감상' are very common.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구가 수업 시간에 자주 농담해요.
examples.en: A classmate of mine often jokes during class.
My uncle joked with a smile at the dinner table.
Don't joke with me like that.
They're someone who likes to joke.
If you joke sometimes, the mood gets better.

examples.ko: 기분 나쁘게 하려고 농담한 게 아니에요.
examples.en: I didn't joke to upset you.

explain: '농담하다'보다 '농담을 하다'라고 더 자주 말해요. 반대말은 '진담'이라서 '농담이에요', '농담이죠?'처럼 짧게도 많이 써요. 윗사람에게는 '농담하지 마세요'가 강하게 들릴 수 있으니 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 농담 반 진담 반으로 한 말인데 친구가 진지하게 받아들였어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃으며 말했지만 속마음도 조금 섞여 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you said something with a smile but part of it was meant seriously.

explain_en: People say '농담을 하다' more often than '농담하다'. The opposite is '진담' (serious talk), and short lines like '농담이에요' and '농담이죠?' are very common. '농담하지 마세요' can sound harsh to someone older, so be careful.

examples.en: Korea exports cars to many countries.
This company exported fruit last year.
It's a product exported overseas, so the packaging is sturdy.
They are exporting seaweed to many countries.
You need a lot of documents to export goods.

examples.ko: 작년에 수출한 양이 두 배가 됐어요.
examples.en: The amount exported last year doubled.

explain: 짝말은 '수입하다'예요. 나라 밖으로 내보내면 '수출', 안으로 들여오면 '수입'이라서 소리가 비슷해 헷갈려요. '출'은 나가는 것, '입'은 들어오는 것으로 기억하세요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '수입하다'. Sending goods out of the country is '수출' and bringing them in is '수입', and the similar sounds are easy to mix up. Remember '출' as going out and '입' as coming in.

examples.en: I print the meeting documents at work.
I printed the photo in a large size.

examples.ko: 인쇄하기 전에 한 번 더 확인하세요.
examples.en: Check once more before you print.
Where is it cheap to print?
Print the ticket and bring it with you.

examples.ko: 프린터가 고장 나서 인쇄할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The printer is broken, so I can't print.

explain: 컴퓨터 파일을 종이로 뽑을 때는 '프린트하다'나 '출력하다'도 많이 써요. '인쇄하다'는 책이나 신문을 많이 찍는 일에도 써요. 이미 있는 종이를 기계로 똑같이 찍는 건 '복사하다'예요.
explain_en: For printing a computer file onto paper, people often say '프린트하다' or '출력하다' too. '인쇄하다' also covers mass printing of books and newspapers. Making a copy of an existing sheet on a machine is '복사하다'.

examples.en: I put on make-up for ten minutes every morning.
I got up late today, so I didn't wear make-up.
My friend put on make-up nicely today.
I want to learn how to put on make-up.
I put on make-up and got dressed to go to the party.
I asked whether I may wear make-up at work.

explain: '화장하다'에는 소리가 같은 '화장(火葬)하다'도 있어서, 장례 이야기에서는 시신을 불에 태운다는 다른 뜻이에요. 얼굴 화장은 '메이크업하다'라고도 하고, 지울 때는 '화장을 지우다'라고 해요. '화장을 하다'처럼 띄어서도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '화장하다' has a sound-alike, '화장(火葬)하다', which in talk about funerals means cremation, so context matters. Face make-up is also called '메이크업하다', and removing it is '화장을 지우다'. People also often say it in two words, '화장을 하다'.

examples.en: My older sister is getting promoted this month.
My father was promoted to department head last year.
If you work hard, you can be promoted.
I was promoted and my pay went up a lot too.
What changes if you get promoted?
I got promoted and moved to a new office.

explain: 직장에서 직급이 올라갈 때만 써요. 월급만 오른 경우는 '월급이 오르다'라고 해요. 새 직급 뒤에 '(으)로'를 붙여서 '과장으로 승진하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Use it only when your rank at work goes up. If only your pay rises, say '월급이 오르다'. The new rank takes '(으)로', as in '과장으로 승진하다'.

examples.en: My mother leaves the hospital tomorrow morning.
My grandfather left the hospital yesterday.
When are you leaving the hospital, teacher?
When you leave the hospital, rest well at home.
The doctor said I may leave the hospital.
My family came to pick me up on the day I left the hospital.

explain: 짝말은 '입원하다'예요. 병원에 들어가면 '입원', 나오면 '퇴원'이고 '병원에서 퇴원하다'처럼 '에서'를 써요. 아직 병원에 있을 때는 '입원 중이에요'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '입원하다'. Entering the hospital is '입원' and leaving is '퇴원', used with '에서' as in '병원에서 퇴원하다'. While someone is still in the hospital, say '입원 중이에요'.

examples.en: I talk over my career path with my parents.
I discussed the travel plans with my friend.

examples.ko: 어려운 일은 혼자 하지 말고 의논하세요.
examples.en: Don't handle difficult things alone; talk them over.
I'll decide after we talk it over as a family.
We need time to discuss it with the team members.
I came because I have something to talk over with you, teacher.

explain: '의논하다'는 같이 정할 일을 이야기할 때 써요. '상의하다'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 병원이나 상담소처럼 전문가에게 고민을 말할 때는 '상담하다'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: Use '의논하다' for talking something through to decide it together. '상의하다' is used almost the same way. When you bring a worry to an expert, like at a clinic or counseling center, '상담하다' fits better.

examples.ko: 저는 밥 먹고 나서 바로 양치질해요.
examples.en: I brush my teeth right after eating.
I was tired yesterday and slept without brushing my teeth.
I brushed my teeth three times today.
Turn off the water while you brush your teeth.
Be sure to brush your teeth before bed.
I took out my toothbrush to brush my teeth.

explain: '양치하다', '이를 닦다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 일상에서는 '이 닦았어?'가 가장 자연스러워요. 아이에게는 '이 닦자'라고 말해요.
explain_en: '양치하다' and '이를 닦다' mean the same thing. In daily talk, '이 닦았어?' is the most natural. To a child you say '이 닦자'.

examples.en: I wash the dishes right after dinner.
I did the dishes today.
I listen to music while I wash the dishes.
After I eat and wash the dishes, I'll clean up.
If we wash the dishes together, it finishes quickly.
Thank you for doing the dishes today.

explain: '설거지'는 식사 뒤에 그릇을 씻어 정리하는 집안일 전체를 가리켜서 '설거지를 하다'라고 많이 말해요. 컵 한 개만 씻을 때는 '컵을 씻다'라고 해요. 가족끼리 순서를 정할 때 '설거지 당번'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '설거지' names the whole chore of washing and putting away dishes after a meal, so '설거지를 하다' is very common. If you only wash one cup, say '컵을 씻다'. Families also use '설거지 당번' for whose turn it is.

examples.en: I sometimes go for a drive to the sea on weekends.
I went for a drive to the Han River with a friend at night.
If the weather is nice, I want to go for a drive.
I listened to songs during the drive.
Do you want to go for a drive together this weekend?
I opened the window and felt the wind while driving around.

explain: '드라이브'는 목적지 없이 즐기려고 차를 타고 다니는 일이에요. 출퇴근처럼 일 때문에 운전하면 '운전하다'라고 해요. 영어 drive와 달리 'drive a car'는 '드라이브'가 아니라 '운전하다'예요.
explain_en: '드라이브' is riding around in a car for fun, often with no set destination. Driving for work or commuting is '운전하다'. Unlike English, 'drive a car' is '운전하다', not '드라이브하다'.

examples.en: I work part-time at a cafe in front of school.
I worked part-time at a convenience store during vacation.
I go to school while working part-time.
The place where I work part-time is close to home.
I'm working part-time at a restaurant every weekend.

examples.ko: 아르바이트해서 모은 돈으로 여행 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I'll travel with the money I saved from part-time work.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 '알바'라고 많이 말하고, '알바해요', '알바생'처럼 써요. 정규직으로 일하는 건 '일하다'나 '근무하다'라고 해요. '아르바이트를 하다'처럼 풀어서도 자주 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk it is shortened to '알바', as in '알바해요' and '알바생' (part-timer). Full-time work is '일하다' or '근무하다'. You can also split it, as in '아르바이트를 하다'.

examples.en: Edison invented the light bulb.
I want to invent a new toy.

examples.ko: 우리 생활을 편하게 하려면 무엇을 발명하면 좋을까요?
examples.en: What should we invent to make our daily lives easier?
Inventing is fun but very difficult.

examples.ko: 이 대회에서는 학생들이 직접 물건을 발명해요.
examples.en: In this contest, students invent things themselves.
Do you know who invented this machine?

explain: 없던 물건이나 기술을 처음 만들어 낼 때 써요. 이미 있던 것을 찾아내면 '발견하다'라서 '뉴턴이 중력을 발견했어요'라고 해요. 그냥 만들 때는 '만들다'를 쓰고, '발명하다'는 새 기술이나 기계에 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it when someone creates a new thing or technology for the first time. Finding something that already existed is '발견하다', as in '뉴턴이 중력을 발견했어요'. For ordinary making, use '만들다'; '발명하다' fits new technology and machines.

examples.en: My older sister gave birth to a healthy baby at the hospital.
My sister-in-law is giving birth next month.
She's resting at home after giving birth.
Her husband was beside her on the day she gave birth.
To give birth, you need to choose a hospital in advance.

examples.ko: 출산할 때 필요한 물건을 미리 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought the things I need for the birth in advance.

explain: '출산하다'는 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스나 병원 안내에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '아기를 낳다'가 더 자연스러워요. 명사로 '출산 휴가', '출산율', '출산 준비'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: '출산하다' is formal and appears in the news and hospital notices. In everyday talk, '아기를 낳다' is more natural. The noun is common in '출산 휴가' (maternity leave), '출산율' (birth rate) and '출산 준비' (birth preparation).

examples.ko: 영어를 잘하는 친구가 저를 위해 통역해요.
examples.en: A friend who speaks English well interprets for me.
I interpreted English into Korean at the meeting.

examples.ko: 말을 바로 통역하는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Interpreting speech on the spot isn't easy.

examples.ko: 한국어를 아주 잘하면 통역할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you speak Korean very well, you can interpret.
Don't worry, I'll interpret for you.
I couldn't eat lunch because I was interpreting.

explain: '통역'은 말을 소리로 바로 옮기는 일이고, 글을 옮기는 일은 '번역'이에요. 그래서 회의에서는 '통역', 책이나 문서는 '번역'이라고 해요. 직업 이름은 '통역사'이고, '통역해 주다'를 자주 써요.
explain_en: '통역' is carrying spoken words across languages on the spot, while moving written text is '번역'. So you use '통역' at meetings and '번역' for books and documents. The job is '통역사', and '통역해 주다' (interpret for someone) is common.

examples.ko: 저는 일주일에 한 번 도서관에 책을 반납해요.
examples.en: I return books to the library once a week.
I returned the umbrella I borrowed yesterday to my friend.
By when do I have to return this book?
If you return it late, you have to pay.
I returned the hotel key and left.

examples.ko: 반납하러 갔는데 도서관 문이 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I went to return it, but the library was closed.

explain: 책, 열쇠, 우산, 렌터카처럼 '빌린 것'을 돌려줄 때 써요. 산 물건을 가게에 돌려주고 돈을 받는 건 '환불하다'예요. 빌린 돈을 돌려줄 때는 '반납하다'가 아니라 '갚다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it for things you borrowed: books, keys, umbrellas, rental cars. Taking a purchase back to a shop for your money is '환불하다'. For borrowed money, use '갚다', not '반납하다'.

examples.en: The mother takes care of her sick child all night.
I took care of my grandmother for three days.

examples.ko: 아픈 친구를 간호하느라 모임에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go to the gathering because I was taking care of my sick friend.
Nursing patients is hard work.
I'm taking care of my father at the hospital.
Because you took care of me, I recovered quickly.

explain: 아픈 사람 곁에서 돌볼 때 쓰고, 병원에서 일하는 직업은 '간호사'예요. 가족이 아픈 사람을 돌볼 때 '병간호'라는 말도 많이 해요. 아이나 노인을 평소에 돌보는 일에는 '돌보다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it for caring for a sick person at their side; the hospital job is '간호사' (nurse). For family caring for a patient, people also say '병간호'. For everyday care of children or older people, use '돌보다'.

examples.en: I get motion sick when I ride a bus for a long time.
I got seasick on the boat yesterday.

examples.ko: 멀미하지 않으려면 출발 전에 약을 먹으세요.
examples.en: To avoid motion sickness, take medicine before you leave.
I seated the carsick child in the front seat.

examples.ko: 차에서 책을 읽으면 멀미할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I get carsick if I read in a car.
I felt sick on the mountain road, so I opened the window.

explain: '멀미가 나다', '멀미를 하다'처럼도 자주 말해요. 탈것 이름을 붙여 '차멀미', '배멀미', '비행기 멀미'라고 하고, 약은 '멀미약'이에요. 속이 울렁거린다는 느낌은 '속이 안 좋아요'로도 말해요.
explain_en: People often say it as '멀미가 나다' or '멀미를 하다'. Attach the vehicle to name it: '차멀미' (carsickness), '배멀미' (seasickness), '비행기 멀미'. The medicine is '멀미약'. You can also describe the feeling as '속이 안 좋아요'.

examples.en: At the hospital I take a number and wait in a chair.
I waited in the lobby for an hour.
Please wait over here for a moment.
There were too many people waiting, so I gave up.
I'll be waiting in the car.
Wait here, and go in when your name is called.

explain: 병원, 은행, 안내방송, 콜센터에서 자주 들어요. 친구에게는 '기다려'가 자연스러워요. '대기 번호', '대기 시간', '대기 중'처럼 붙여서도 많이 써요.
explain_en: You hear it a lot at hospitals, banks, announcements and call centers. With a friend, '기다려' is more natural. It also attaches to other words: '대기 번호' (queue number), '대기 시간' (waiting time), '대기 중' (on standby).

examples.ko: 저는 모르는 것이 있으면 선생님께 도움을 요청해요.
examples.en: If there's something I don't know, I ask the teacher for help.
I asked the hotel for more towels.
If you need it, ask anytime.
I don't really know how to make a request.

examples.ko: 다시 한번 설명해 달라고 요청하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to ask them to explain once more.
I sent the documents you requested by email today.

explain: 가까운 사이에는 '부탁하다', 호텔·회사·이메일처럼 공식적인 상황에서는 '요청하다'를 써요. '요청 사항', '요청을 받다'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요. '요구하다'는 당연히 해 달라는 느낌이라 더 강해요.
explain_en: Between people who are close, use '부탁하다'; in formal settings like hotels, companies and emails, use '요청하다'. The noun appears in '요청 사항' (requests) and '요청을 받다' (receive a request). '요구하다' is stronger, as if demanding something owed.

examples.en: I record my day in a diary every day.
I wrote down the lesson in my notebook.
If you write it down right away, it's easy to remember later.
I want to record what happened on the trip.

examples.ko: 저는 모든 일을 기록하는 습관이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of recording everything.

examples.ko: 어제 기록한 내용을 지금 읽어 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll read the notes I recorded yesterday now.

explain: '적다'는 가볍게 메모할 때, '기록하다'는 남겨 두려고 정리해서 쓸 때 써요. 사진이나 영상으로 남기는 것도 '기록하다'라고 해요. 명사 '기록'은 스포츠에서 '신기록'처럼도 쓰여요.
explain_en: '적다' is for jotting something down lightly; '기록하다' is for writing it up so it is kept. Saving something in photos or video is also '기록하다'. The noun '기록' appears in sports too, as in '신기록' (new record).
